# PEN-4357 — backfill the $HOME tooling directories behind the wrapper lead, so the PVC dotfiles cannot promote them past it

`src/server/job-manifest.ts`, in `buildEnvVars()`, beside the PEN-3713/PEN-3732
prepend: after `IMAGE_WRAPPER_BIN_DIR` is made `PATH[0]`, also ensure
`<merged.HOME>/.local/bin` and `<merged.HOME>/bin` are PRESENT behind it,
inserted immediately after the lead when absent. `src/server/job-manifest.test.ts`
gains five bash-resolution cases plus a control; two existing exact-equality
cases are updated and the idempotence case is strengthened to a fixed point.

## Supersedes the "Not covered" paragraph of pen-3714-wrapper-path-order.md

That entry closed with: *"the snippet is not the last writer of `PATH` overall.
The tool shells `claude` spawns source `$HOME/.bashrc` (via the `BASH_ENV` stub)
… so a `PATH` prepend written there demotes the wrapper directory again. That
later writer is outside this change."* It was right, and this is that later
writer being brought inside. The directory here is append-only, so that entry
stays as written; read it with this one.

## Why the prepend alone was not enough

PEN-3713 made the wrapper directory `PATH[0]` **on the Job's process env**. That
env is not what the agent's commands resolve under. The PVC shell dotfiles
(`$HOME/.bashrc`, `.profile`, `.zshenv` — fleet state, not in this repo) each
carry a presence-guarded prepend:

```sh
case ":$PATH:" in
  *":$HOME/.local/bin:"*) ;;
  *) PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH" ;;
esac
```

and the same shape for `$HOME/bin`. This manifest points `BASH_ENV` (and
`ZDOTDIR`) at stubs that chain them on **every non-interactive shell**, so the
stanza is a later writer than the prepend, running in the Job's own shell.

The guard is on PRESENCE. So an `adapterConfig.env.PATH` that merely OMITS
`<base>/.local/bin` does not take the directory out of the lookup — it moves it
to the **front**, ahead of the root-owned wrappers. The live layer-4 value is
exactly that shape: the chart default with `/paperclip/.local/bin` swapped for
`/paperclip/opencode-api-key-bin`.

## Measured, not inferred

Agent pod `ac-29033747-…`, image `sha-6b81856-k8s-vendored`, PVC
`paperclip-data`, 2026-10-19:

| shell | `gh` resolves to | writable by uid 1000 |
|---|---|---|
| top-level tool shell | `/usr/local/libexec/paperclip/bin/gh` | no |
| `sh -c` (dash, no `BASH_ENV`) | `/usr/local/libexec/paperclip/bin/gh` | no |
| **`bash -c`** | **`/paperclip/.local/bin/gh`** (`node:node 755`) | **yes** |

Same for `git` and `github-mcp-server`. Reproduced in an A/B against the real
`/paperclip/.bashrc`: with the two directories backfilled behind the lead, all
three resolve to the image directory.

Severity is tamperability, not bypass. Both copies chain the same egress
runtime (`cmp` against the image: `gh` byte-identical; `git` and
`github-mcp-server` differ only in which chained path they name), so
PEN-2527/3152/3156 still applied. What was wrong is that the wrappers actually
executing were uid-1000-writable on a PVC shared across companies — the
PEN-3713 threat model, on the traffic path.

## Why here and not in the N config values

The omission originated in `adapterConfig.env.PATH`, an operator-set database
value, and configuration is not a security control. This is the adapter-layer
mirror of `paperclip.toolingBinDirs` in the chart, which separates the same two
concerns ("directories that must lead" vs "directories that must be present")
for the StatefulSet and api Deployment. Keyed off `merged.HOME` rather than the
data mount, because `$HOME` is what the stanza itself expands — deriving it from
the mount would miss an isolated per-run home.

## What this does NOT close

The same dotfiles also carry **unconditional** `export PATH="$BUN_INSTALL/bin:$PATH"`
lines. No presence invariant can neutralise those, and `/paperclip/.bun/bin` is
agent-writable and leads the final PATH. It is harmless today only because that
directory carries no `gh`/`git`/`github-mcp-server` — an observation about
current PVC contents, not a control. More fundamentally `/paperclip/.bashrc`
itself is `node:node 664`, so an agent that rewrites it controls every later
shell's PATH outright. Closing that class needs the dotfiles to stop being
agent-writable; filed as PEN-4367. This change removes the exposure that is
live today under the *benign* dotfiles, and is a precondition for PEN-3840
step 4 (deleting the stale PVC wrappers) not to delete the evidence while
leaving the exposure.

## Read the new tests together

`gh`/`git`/`github-mcp-server` under `bash -c` assert RESOLUTION against the
PATH this manifest actually emits from the live operator value, with the
verbatim stanza and a `BASH_ENV` stub of the same shape the manifest ships.
The control re-runs the identical harness on the PATH the implementation
emitted *before* this change and requires `agent-writable-pvc` — without it a
harness that silently never reached the stanza would pass the other cases
vacuously. The inherited-PATH case covers the harder shape where both stanzas
fire. The fixed-point case replaces the old idempotence case: the first build
now legitimately adds two entries, so "unchanged on the first build" no longer
catches the PATH-growth bug that case existed for.

Verified by mutation, not assumed: with the backfill removed, four
resolution cases fail with `expected 'agent-writable-pvc' to be 'image-wrapper'`
and the control still passes.

## The chart test does not cover this

`deploy/helm/paperclip/tests/agent-egress-path.test.mjs` already runs the
stanza (`resolvesThroughDotfile`) — that part of PEN-4357's filing was wrong and
is corrected on the card. But it runs it against the chart-RENDERED PATH, which
carries the tooling directories by construction, and never against the Job PATH
`buildEnvVars()` emits from an operator-set value. The gap was coverage, not
technique.
